title: Content Plan
subtitle: 150 days · marathoner → sprinter
premise: The brand isn't 'fitness influencer'. It's **test subject**. You put your own body through things — historical diets, elite standards, a transformation with a deadline — and you publish the numbers whether they flatter you or not.

That framing is what lets one channel hold a Viking diet video, a Navy SEAL fitness test and a sprint transformation without feeling scattered. Everything is the same question: what can a body actually do, and how do we know?
It also gives you the one thing most fitness accounts never get — a reason to keep watching. Not tips. A story with an ending.

spine.name: The Quest — marathoner to sprinter
spine.why: You ran Gold Coast in July. Every adaptation in your body right now is the wrong one for sprinting: slow-twitch dominant, low power output, trained for economy instead of force. That conflict IS the hook — you're not starting from zero, you're starting from the wrong place. Nobody else can make that video, because it's true about you and not about them.
spine.targetNote: Set the exact number AFTER Day 1 baseline — a target you miss publicly is a better story than one you sandbagged, but the claim has to be real. Roughly: sub-13s is fit, sub-12s is genuinely top few percent of adult men, sub-11s is club-athlete territory. Verify before you say '1%' on camera; a number you can defend beats a number that gets you ratio'd.

phases.name: Baseline & rebuild
phases.focus: Film every test on Day 1. Then 4 weeks of tendon and hamstring prep BEFORE any max-effort sprinting. This phase is not optional.
phases.story: The marathon body is the problem

phases.name: Power
phases.focus: Heavy lower body, plyometrics, hill sprints. Bodyweight will go up — that's content, not failure.

phases.name: Speed
phases.focus: Max velocity work, flying 30s, sprint mechanics. First real time drops land here.
phases.story: The first time it actually feels fast

phases.name: Sharpen
phases.focus: Block starts, acceleration, race modelling. Times get stubborn — that's the mid-story slump you film honestly.

phases.name: Peak & trial
phases.focus: Taper, then the filmed public time trial. Invite people. Stakes on camera.

spine.risk: Sprinting off an endurance base is the single highest hamstring-tear risk in athletics. If you tear one in week three, the entire 150-day arc dies with it and there's no channel. Four weeks of progressive acceleration work before anything maximal. This is the one place where being impatient costs you everything.

pillars.name: The Quest
pillars.what: The sprint transformation. Weekly long-form episode + daily diary shorts pulled from the same footage.
pillars.why: Narrative spine. Builds the returning audience and the watch hours.

pillars.name: Ancient Protocols
pillars.what: 24 hours (sometimes 7 days) eating and training as a historical warrior culture.
pillars.why: Highest virality per hour of effort you own. Weird, searchable, argument-provoking, cheap to film.

pillars.name: The Standard
pillars.what: Putting yourself through elite, military and historical fitness tests. Pass or fail, on camera.
pillars.why: Built-in stakes and a built-in ending. People watch to see if you make it.

pillars.name: Debunk
pillars.what: Myth checks where you're the guinea pig, not the lecturer.
pillars.why: Comment bait and credibility. Cheapest thing you can film.

pillars.name: Real Life
pillars.what: Brisbane, the markets, NRICH, the actual grind behind the training.
pillars.why: Mostly stories. This is the trust layer — it's what turns viewers into people who care whether you hit sub-12.

hook: First 1.5 seconds decide everything. Number + stake + conflict: 'I ran a marathon 4 weeks ago. Today I'm trying to break 12 seconds.'
Cold open on the most visually strange moment. Never open on your face talking.
On-screen text mirrors the spoken hook — most people watch muted.
Never 'hey guys', never 'in this video', never an intro.
retention: State the open loop in the first 3 seconds and don't resolve it until the end.
Cut every 1.5–2.5 seconds. If nothing changed on screen for 3 seconds, you lost them.
Keep a number visible — a timer, the scale, the plate count. It gives people a reason to stay for the reveal.
Film the failures. Failure outperforms success almost every time, and it's the thing that makes the wins believable.
shares: Argument bait: 'Roman soldiers ate better than you do' — people share to disagree.
Identity bait: 'if you've ever run a marathon you'll know why this is so hard'.
Steal-ability: one thing they could actually do tomorrow.
Let the comments choose the next diet. Ownership converts watchers into a following.
series: Number every post — 'Day 41 of 150'. It advertises that there's a story and that they've missed some.
End every episode teasing the next one specifically, not vaguely.
Same title format per series so the algorithm and the audience both learn to recognise it.

rhythm.note: 2 reels a day is 300 posts over 150 days. You cannot film that live — the whole system is batching and buffer. Rule: never post footage you shot today. Bank never drops below 14 posts.

days.what: Plan the week, script the long form, pick Thursday's 12 shorts
SHOOT 1 — long-form A-roll + the training session in it (one shoot should yield 6–10 shorts as by-product)
Edit long form. Mark every moment that could stand alone as a short.
SHOOT 2 — batch 8–12 shorts. This day is what keeps the buffer alive.
Edit + schedule the next 7 days of reels
Publish long form (9am). Market day — film real-life content while you're there.
Market. Evening: review the numbers, pick next week.

Ancient Protocols: 24h as a Roman legionary — ~70% grain, posca, cheese. 'Rome conquered the world on porridge.'
24h as a Spartan — black broth (pork, blood, vinegar). Famously the worst food in the ancient world.
24h as a Viking — skyr, dried cod, ale, no vegetables at all
24h as a Mongol horse archer — mare's milk, dried meat, and yes, the blood
24h as a gladiator — barley and ash. They were deliberately fat. Nobody knows this.
24h as a samurai — rice, miso, fish, no meat. They were also 5'3".
24h as an Aztec eagle warrior — chia, amaranth, spirulina. Accidentally a modern superfood stack.
24h as an ancient Olympian — Milo of Croton reportedly ate 9kg of meat a day
24h as a Victorian strongman — raw eggs, milk, steak, no vegetables
24h as a Zulu impi warrior — amasi and maize, then run 50km
7 days on the Roman diet — the long-form version once the 24h one hits
I ate 6,000 calories like an Olympic swimmer
The Standard: The Roman legionary march — 30km in 5 hours carrying 20kg
Navy SEAL PST — can a marathon runner pass?
The NFL combine — every test, as a distance runner
The Cooper test — 12 minutes, elite standard
Ancient Olympic pentathlon — all five events in one day
Firefighter physical ability test in full kit
1896 Olympic gold medal standards — could you have medalled?

Answering the comment that said I'd never do it

watch: 3-second retention — want 70%+ on shorts. Below 60% means the hook failed, not the video.
Shares per view — the single best predictor of a post breaking out
Average view duration on long form — the number that builds the monetisation path
rules: Any format that hits 3× your baseline views: make 3 more within 7 days. Ride it hard.
Any format that underperforms 3 times in a row: drop it, don't 'fix' it.
Never judge a post before 72 hours — shorts routinely spike late.
Post consistency beats post quality at this stage. A 7/10 posted daily beats a 9/10 posted weekly.

money.note: Optimise for virality now — but build so the money works later without a jarring pivot.
points: YouTube Partner Program, shorts route: 1,000 subs + 10 million shorts views in 90 days. At 2 reels/day that's the realistic path.
Long-form route: 1,000 subs + 4,000 watch hours in 12 months. The weekly episode is what builds this — shorts alone won't.
Pre-workout affiliate isn't live yet: don't mention a brand and don't sign any competing supplement deal in the meantime.
Do start showing pre-workout in training footage now, unbranded. When the deal lands it reads as continuity instead of a sellout moment.
Ad revenue follows watch time, not views. That's the argument for never dropping the weekly long form even when shorts are carrying the growth.

launch.note: First 14 days. Get these filmed and banked before Day 1 if you can.
